vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ecommerce-review-analyzer
Version: 1.0.4

The skill is a legitimate tool designed to scrape and analyze e-commerce reviews from platforms like Taobao and JD. It uses standard Python libraries (jieba, python-docx, fpdf2) and relies on the host's built-in browser automation to perform its stated functions. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious code execution, or harmful prompt injection was found in SKILL.md or the associated metadata.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (browser-based scraping and analysis of e-commerce reviews); it requests only a Python runtime and uses the platform browser session, which is expected for this task.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (e-commerce review analysis for Taobao/JD/Pinduoduo) matches the instructions: browser automation to scrape logged-in reviews, Chinese NLP (jieba), and generation of .docx/.pdf reports. Required binary (python3) and Python packages are appropriate for producing reports and Chinese text analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly requires OpenClaw built-in browser automation and states the browser session will inherit the user's logged-in state. This is necessary to scrape reviews behind login, but it means the skill will access the user's authenticated browser session and any pages reachable through it (including potentially PII). The instructions do not request unrelated files, credentials, or external upload endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec or code files). The SKILL.md lists a 'pip install jieba python-docx fpdf2' dependency string — the agent may execute pip at runtime. No archive downloads or external/untrusted URLs are used. Runtime pip installs are normal for Python tools but can change the execution environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested. The lack of additional secrets is proportionate to the described functionality. The only sensitive access is via the browser automation (inherited session), which is expected but should be treated as privileged.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced-always, and it does not declare persistent system-wide changes. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other high-risk requests. There is no evidence the skill modifies other skills or system configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for scraping and analyzing Chinese e-commerce reviews, but it requires use of the platform's browser automation and will access your authenticated browser session. That means it can see any pages or account data the browser is logged into. Before installing or running: 1) only run against accounts/sites you trust or test accounts; 2) be aware scraped reviews may contain PII — review outputs carefully before sharing; 3) note the skill may run 'pip install' at runtime to fetch Python packages from PyPI — if you have policies about installing packages, review them first; 4) if you need stronger guarantees (no access to your real accounts), request a version that accepts pre-exported review files instead of live browser scraping. Overall the skill is internally consistent, but treat browser-inherited session access as sensitive privilege.
